title: From a finite module Tor bound to a bounded augmented projective model
statement: Let $S$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $M$ a finitely generated $S$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and $d\geq0$ an integer. Suppose $\operatorname{Tor}^S_j(M,N)=0$ for every $S$-module $N$ and every $j>d$, using first-variable Tor [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. Work in the ordinary module derived category $D(S)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with derived tensor computed as in [lem-pc-source-kflat-module-tensor-model]. Then $H^i(M[0]\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}N[0])=0$ for every $S$-module $N$ and every $i\notin[-d,0]$. There are a cochain complex $E^\bullet$ of finitely generated projective $S$-modules [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], with $E^i=0$ for $i\notin[-d,0]$, and an augmentation $\varepsilon:E^0\to M$ such that $E^\bullet\to M[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Explicitly, $\varepsilon$ is surjective, $\ker\varepsilon=\operatorname{im}(d_E^{-1})$, and $\ker(d_E^i)=\operatorname{im}(d_E^{i-1})$ for every $i<0$; writing $F_j=E^{-j}$ gives an exact augmented resolution $$0\to F_d\to\cdots\to F_0\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}M\to0.$$ In particular $M[0]$ is perfect [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. When $d=0$, the assertion includes an isomorphism $E^0\cong M$. The zero module and zero ring are allowed.

source.place: Tags 0658, lemma-perfect (model with the specified Tor interval), and 066Q, lemma-perfect-module (augmented finite-projective resolution); ordinary Tor-to-derived-amplitude input via a finite-free resolution.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-free-resolution-noetherian] to $S,M$. Reverse its exact augmented chain resolution to obtain a cochain complex $P$ with $P^{-j}=S^{\oplus n_j}$ for $j\ge0$ and $P^i=0$ for $i>0$. Its augmentation to $M[0]$ induces $H^0(P)\cong M$ and $H^i(P)=0$ for $i\ne0$, directly from the stated kernel-image equalities. Thus it is a quasi-isomorphism. This bounded-above finite-free model proves that $M[0]$ is pseudo-coherent by [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex].

For each $S$-module $N$, apply [lem-kun-derived-module-tor-comparison] with $R=S$. If $i>0$, take $k=-i<0$ to obtain $H^i(M[0]\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}N[0])=0$. If $i<-d$, take $k=-i>d$; the same comparison identifies this cohomology with $\operatorname{Tor}^S_k(M,N)$, which is zero by hypothesis. Hence the derived tensor vanishes outside $[-d,0]$ for every $N$; this is exactly the Tor-amplitude hypothesis required in the next step. No flatness assumption on $N$ has been used.

source.place: Section computing-tor, equation-derived-tensor-module and satellite formula; Tags 00LY (algebra-section-tor), 00LZ (algebra-lemma-tor-welldefined).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-pseudo-coherent-tor-projective-window] with $A=S$, $C=M[0]$, $a=-d$, and $b=0$. The inequality $-d\le0$ follows from $d\ge0$; pseudo-coherence and the required tests on all modules were proved in steps 1 and 2. We obtain $E$ supported in $[-d,0]$ and an isomorphism $Q(E)\cong M[0]$ in $D(S)$, each $E^i$ being a direct summand of a finite free module, hence finite projective as stated by the cited result.

source.place: Tag 0658, lemma-perfect, final assertion with the specified Tor interval.

proof.text: Apply the cohomology functors of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] to this isomorphism. They give $H^0(E)\cong M$ and $H^i(E)=0$ for $i\ne0$. Since $E^1=0$, one has $H^0(E)=E^0/\operatorname{im}d_E^{-1}$. Define $\varepsilon$ as this quotient map followed by the resulting isomorphism to $M$. It is surjective with kernel $\operatorname{im}d_E^{-1}$; it annihilates $d_E^{-1}$, so with zero components in all other degrees it is a cochain map $E\to M[0]$. Its cohomology maps are isomorphisms, so it is a quasi-isomorphism. For $i<0$, vanishing of $H^i(E)=\ker d_E^i/\operatorname{im}d_E^{i-1}$ gives the claimed kernel-image equality. If $d>0$, the equality at $i=-d$ and $E^{-d-1}=0$ give injectivity at the left end; reversing indices therefore gives the displayed exact augmented resolution. If $d=0$, $E^{-1}=0$, so $\varepsilon$ is both surjective and injective and $E^0\cong M$. The bounded finite-projective representative makes $M[0]$ perfect by [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. These constructions also apply to zero modules and the zero ring.
